claims.text: Equiatomic Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 can achieve yield strength above 1000 MPa and total elongation above 15% at room temperature.
The proposed HIP, cold-rolling, annealing, solution-treatment, and quenching route will produce discrete B2 precipitates and a heterogeneous grain structure in Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20.
The target microstructure consists of discrete, coherent B2-ordered precipitates embedded in a continuous, weakly ordered BCC matrix.
Discrete B2 precipitates strengthen the alloy by obstructing dislocation motion.
A heterogeneous grain structure generates back stress and increased strain hardening, thereby improving ductility.
An inverted microstructure with discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix permits matrix plastic flow and suppresses catastrophic brittle fracture.
Lattice distortion in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr provides intrinsic solid-solution strengthening.
Screw dislocations are responsible for room-temperature plasticity in TiZrHfNbTa.
Mo and Nb have sufficiently similar atomic radius and valence that replacing Nb with Mo maintains BCC stability and comparable deformation mechanisms.
Replacing Nb with Mo reduces the density of the equiatomic alloy by approximately 10–15% relative to TiZrHfNbTa.
The processed Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 alloy will have a density of approximately 11–12 g/cm3.
Reducing the volume fraction of the dense ordered phase will mitigate the alloy's density limitation.
Minor Al or Si additions could provide further density reduction if microstructural optimization is insufficient.
As-cast equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr is BCC single-phase or multiphase and has coarse grains.
Screw-dislocation locking at room temperature can make as-cast Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr brittle.
As-cast equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr typically has yield strength above 1500 MPa and elongation below 5%.
A continuous ordered B2 phase promotes brittleness in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Annealing must prevent B2 precipitates from coalescing into a continuous brittle network while also avoiding complete B2 dissolution and loss of strength.
The approach becomes less effective when stacking-fault energy is low enough to cause twinning-induced cracking or high enough to prevent dislocation pile-up.
The processed alloy will reach 1100–1300 MPa yield strength, 1400–1600 MPa tensile strength, 15–25% total elongation, and above 10% uniform elongation without brittle fracture.
